title: Confinement schemas and the reach of block certificates for powers of rational numbers modulo one
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of the second paper on the sets Z_{p/q}(s, s+t) = {ξ > 0 : {ξ(p/q)ⁿ} ∈ [s, s+t) for all n ≥ 0}, the generalized Z-numbers of Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington. The first paper built a corpus of block certificates for individual statements Z_{p/q}(U) = ∅. This paper replaces parts of that corpus by theorems, and then asks what the certificate format can and cannot reach. Thirty certificates in the regime p > q² collapse into one closed-form criterion on the single real parameter ε = {(p−q)s}, settling a set of positions of measure 1 − 2q²/(p(p+q)) at every base and for every real ξ ≠ 0; the criterion extends to a family indexed by a depth K, identified with the finiteness criterion of [FLP95] and with the parameter intervals J¹_b of [Bug04], the depth playing the role of the denominator of the rotation number. An explicit escape time for L ≤ ξ ≤ X is extracted from the soundness proof, and every unranked certificate of [Ste26] is made effective by it. A completeness theorem says the verdict is forced on the class where a certificate can exist — a finite hold set — and that an infinite hold set refuses every unranked certificate at every depth and over every denominator, which turns a bounded computer search into a theorem. A measure-theoretic depth–size bound 1 ≤ 2δ(K + 2 + log_{p/q} 2B) prices [KK17, Prob. 6.1] for this format. Finally a rank-stratified certificate gives ‖ξ(3/2)ⁿ‖ < 2/7 = 0.285714… infinitely often for every ξ ≠ 0, past the 31/81 = 0.38271… of [Dub19] as a window and past the corpus's own 1/3 as a nearest-integer constant.
